summary: Cut strip is stable, but the kick impact at 103.06-103.13 has a white flash with a big pose pop, and the kick leg and the spinning body look stiff and sliding.

faults.what: Between 103.03 and 103.09 the whole frame washes to a flat white-grey overlay. The kicker jumps from standing to a high leg while the red-shirt figure goes from upright to tipped over head-first. There are no in-between poses, and by 103.13 he is horizontal and far lower in the frame. The kick contact is never seen, so the hit does not read.
faults.fix: Add 2-3 in-between frames of the kick connecting and the victim's reaction. Make the flash a shorter, partial-opacity pulse instead of a full-frame wash.

faults.what: The kicker's leg stays rigidly straight and vertical from 103.13 to 103.26 with no follow-through or settle. The victim flies off flat and horizontal, with no anticipation or hip lead, and his limbs trail stiffly. It reads as a prop launched, not a spin like a top.
faults.fix: Add a body rotation or spin to the victim, with a little overshoot and settle on the kicker's leg.

faults.what: The victim is cut off at the right edge of the frame by 103.19-103.26. The orange rings and spark bursts overlap his head and torso and hide the silhouette, so the spin is hard to read.
faults.fix: Move the rings behind him or shrink them, and keep the victim inside the frame.

faults.what: In the cut-in frames 100.83-101.06 the pair are nearly frozen in a stiff hands-pushing pose. Only tiny drift is visible, so it reads as mushy and not as a held beat. The left figure is also mostly out of frame and cut off.
faults.fix: Hold a clearer pose, or add a small anticipation move before the kick. Reframe so the kicker is in shot.
